claim: Persona's platform is built on six core objects: Inquiry (one identity-verification interaction producing approved/declined/needs-review), Verification (a specific check), Account (container grouping all data for a person or business), Report (external data pulls), Case (container for manual review), and Workflow (automation responding to events). Common use cases named: KYC onboarding, age verification, fraud prevention, trust and safety.
notes: Also documents integration methods: Hosted Flow, Embedded Flow, Mobile SDKs, and backend-only Transactions API.

claim: Workflows support three trigger types (Persona events, API triggers with configurable input schemas, scheduled triggers) plus manual and workflow-to-workflow triggering, and four step types (action, wait, parallel, conditional). Conditional steps express if/then/else routes referencing inquiry criteria (age, country, government ID number, selfie liveness score), report criteria (watchlist/adverse-media/synthetic-fraud results), case status, account tags, template criteria, database-match criteria, and third-party data ingested via API triggers or custom code.
notes: Conditional routes are ordered with at least one Route and an Else branch (help article 4q44atlPvZvBNZAbYJzi3f). No cross-rule priority/conflict-resolution system is documented; logic is an explicit flow graph.

claim: The workflow action library includes: Approve Inquiry, Decline Inquiry, Mark Inquiry for Review, Create Case, Create Inquiry, Run Report, Run Workflow, Add Item to List, Evaluate Code (custom JavaScript with typed return values), Make HTTPS Request (POST/GET with HMAC Persona-Signature), Redact Object (field-level and conditional redaction), Send Email (custom SMTP), Send SMS, Send Slack Message, Tag Object, Trust Device, Update Hubspot/Salesforce/Zendesk.
notes: Evaluate Code step is gated to Growth and Enterprise plans per help article 7eNHMEGyHPLu35oakfyo79. Wait steps capped at 30 days; longer waits via Scheduled trigger + Schedule Workflow Run action (workflows-best-practices).

claim: Inquiries move through a documented lifecycle with post-inquiry decision statuses approved / declined / needs review, set either by automated post-inquiry workflows applying business logic, by manual reviewer action, or via API endpoints (Approve an Inquiry, Decline an Inquiry, Mark for Review). Every status change emits an event (inquiry.approved, inquiry.declined, inquiry.marked-for-review) usable to trigger webhooks and workflows.
notes: This is Persona's native allow/deny/review output model, at the level of an identity flow rather than an arbitrary business action.

claim: Each verification type has a set of configurable 'verification checks'; each check can be set required or non-required, and all required checks must pass for the verification to pass. Example configurations: which government ID types to accept, whether front+back required, whether to reject IDs previously submitted by other accounts in the organization. Checks are classified as user-behavior or fraud checks. Default required-check sets exist and Persona will 'work with you to configure the defaults'.
notes: The full checks table is only visible inside the customer Dashboard. Tuning defaults is partly a contact-us/CSM-assisted process, indicating services involvement for advanced configuration.

claim: The Verification API returns a per-check array where each check has name, status (passed/failed/not_applicable), requirement (required/not_required/requires_retry), reasons (list of reason strings explaining failure, sometimes carrying underlying vendor signals such as IPQS/Google Web Risk values), and free-form metadata.
notes: Machine-readable reason codes exist at check level; a help article lists verification check fail reasons.

claim: Verification types include Government ID (with NFC variant), Selfie (liveness + face match), Document (utility bill/bank statement), Database (public/private identity records), Phone Number, Email Address, and authoritative database verifications: AAMVA (US driver's licenses), eCBSV (SSA), TIN (US IRS records), Phone Carrier (AT&T/T-Mobile/Verizon), and Serpro (Brazil). Types are mixed and matched within one inquiry to meet 'risk thresholds, compliance requirements, and user experience goals'.
notes: A per-country database coverage map is referenced in the Dashboard. TIN/IRS matching is a building block relevant to winner tax workflows, though Persona has no tax-reporting product.

claim: Reports pull external data about a person or business: Watchlist, PEP, Adverse Media, Business Watchlist, Business Adverse Media, Crypto Address Watchlist, Email Risk, Phone Risk, Address Lookup, plus many more report types visible in the event catalog (synthetic fraud, social media, FINRA broker check, SEC action lookup, business registrations, nonprofit status, community safety). Report templates are saved configurations for repeatable runs.
notes: Match/dismiss lifecycle (watchlist.matched, watchlist.dismissed events) supports screening adjudication.

claim: Continuous report monitoring runs eligible reports (person/business Watchlist, person/business Adverse Media, PEP, Crypto Address Watchlist, Business Nonprofit) on a recurring schedule configurable from 1 to 365 days for perpetual KYC; runs auto-halt when a match is found until the match is dismissed; pause/resume available via dashboard and API. Available only on Growth and Enterprise plans.
notes: Temporal capability is recurring re-screening, not effective-dated policy rules.

claim: Cases is a manual-review/investigation product with a configurable UI, built-in analytics (SLAs and case resolution rates), automations, queues, and assignment. The API supports create, retrieve, update (attach arbitrary external JSON data), add/remove Persona objects, assign, set status, tag, search, and redact. Webhook events include case.assigned, case.queue-updated, case.sla-expired, case.resolved, case.reopened, case.exported, and case.agent-reviewed.
notes: Usage example spans onboarding review, account takeover investigation, fraud investigation, and transaction-monitoring review.

claim: Case Templates define per-template custom field schemas (array, boolean, choices, date, datetime, email-address and more) with per-field required flags, write-policy (none or write_once, rejecting overwrites once set), redaction-policy (none/never), alias source key paths, and custom resolutions; case statuses are fully customizable and typed as initial, intermediate, or end.
notes: Status typing (initial/intermediate/end) documented on the Cases API overview page (docs.withpersona.com/api-reference/cases).

claim: Case Actions are one-click operations for reviewers: Workflow Actions ('anything a Workflow or custom code can do can become a Case Action', e.g. run reports, update accounts, add to lists, send inquiry links, make HTTP requests to re-enable users in external systems) and System Actions (update fields/tags, modify queue assignments, set SLA deadlines, redact PII). Actions are configured in the Case template and attached to buttons, data tables, or resource modules.
notes: Human decisions can push effects into external systems synchronously with case resolution.

claim: Persona offers an AML case management and SAR filing solution: Alert Cases and SAR Investigation Cases with fully customizable status progressions (e.g. Open -> Under Review -> Ready for BSA Officer Review -> Submitted to FinCEN), adjustable SLA deadlines, notification reminders, role-based permission controls, configurable investigation checklists, and SAR export as XML or direct electronic filing to FinCEN via SDTM. The event catalog includes sar.created and sar.filed.
page_title: AML Case Management & SAR Filing Overview (Help Center)
notes: Direct regulator-facing filing workflow (FinCEN SDTM). SAR events corroborated at docs.withpersona.com/events.

claim: Case statuses support governance controls: the status switcher can be disabled until defined conditions are met, and Status Tags let agents record a required 'reason for status change' when approving/declining/updating a case, with tags markable as required per status.
notes: Reason-coded human decisions; supports decision-quality metrics.

claim: Workflows are versioned with change management: edits create drafts; publishing creates a locked, immutable version; full version history with editable descriptions; revert to any prior version; and percentage-based staged rollouts where a chosen share of new runs use the new version (treatment) while the rest use the previous version (control), with the Runs table showing which version processed each run. Each Workflow Run has a workflow-version relationship in the API.
page_title: Workflow Versions and Change Management (Help Center)
notes: Corroborated by 'Testing and auditing your Workflows' (help article 6hnq0KFsYB3Edjt9ME4E9), 'Managing Workflow versions and state', the workflow.published event, and the workflow-version relationship on POST /workflows/{id}/trigger responses.

claim: Inquiry Templates are versioned: every change creates a new immutable published version (itmplv_ IDs); integrations can pin to a specific version or track the latest (itmpl_); 'Each Inquiry is permanently linked to the version of the Inquiry Template that was live when it was generated'; version history supports comparison against previous versions and reverting.
page_title: Inquiry Template Versions and Change Management (Help Center)
notes: Also documented at docs.withpersona.com/inquiry-templates. Verification templates have an equivalent versioning article (75eRhQOPuENRVm6qzkS6qp).

claim: Graph is a link-analysis product that queries all Persona accounts for shared data (emails, IPs, device fingerprints, government ID numbers, faces) to surface fraud rings; queries can be saved as parameterized Graph Query Templates, run ad hoc, via API (POST /graph-queries with a parameter-map), from Account and Case views (with historical snapshot comparison), or automatically inside Workflow conditionals for 'automated rules and decisioning based on graph data'. Customers can enrich accounts with external data for use in queries.
notes: Query API is async (submitted -> completed) with node limits; results include node lists and an explorer-url.

claim: Lists flag inquiries matching predefined values and workflows can automatically approve, decline, or flag on list match. Supported list types: browser fingerprint, device fingerprint, email address, geolocation, government ID number, IP address, name, phone number, string, country, and face (face lists via support enablement). Lists are managed via dashboard, API, and bulk importers.
notes: Country and geolocation lists enable jurisdiction-based allow/deny logic in workflows; this is customer-authored, not Persona-shipped legal content.

claim: Transactions are generic, customer-defined event objects that 'capture some event associated with that user/entity' (e.g. onboarding, loan application): Transaction Types define custom field schemas (Boolean, Date, Documents, File, Float, Hash, Integer, String, Multiple Choices, Array) and custom statuses; workflows update transaction status through the lifecycle; 'one object provides source of truth on what decision gets made'. Transactions enable API-only integrations (Enterprise plans) where verifications, reports, and decisions run without any Persona UI.
notes: Getting started requires contacting Persona support engineering. This is the closest primitive to modeling arbitrary regulated actions; decisioning over it is asynchronous workflow processing, not a synchronous authorization endpoint.

claim: The API is versioned with dated releases (2020-05-18 through 2025-12-08); versions are set per API key and per webhook, overridable per request via Persona-Version header; a documented breaking vs non-breaking change policy and changelog exist. All POSTs accept Idempotency-Key (24h retention, parameter comparison). Rate limits: default 300 req/min per production environment plus per-product creation quotas, exposed via RateLimit/Quota response headers and a dashboard page. API Logs retain full request/response for 2 weeks with Request-Id tracing, accessible via dashboard and API. Events are listable via GET /events. An OpenAPI 3.1 spec is published (172 paths).
page_title: Versioning / Idempotence / Rate Limiting / API Logs
notes: Composite claim across docs.withpersona.com/versioning, /idempotence, /rate-limiting, /api-logs, /openapi.json. Evidence-export endpoints: Print Inquiry PDF, Print Report PDF, Print Verification PDF.

claim: Webhooks support HMAC-SHA256 signatures, event filters, payload allowlists, attribute blocklists (strip PII), custom HTTP headers, OAuth 2.0 client-credentials authentication for outbound deliveries, event simulation for testing, 7 retries with exponential backoff, manual redelivery from dashboard, per-webhook API versioning, and a 30-day event retention policy. Workflow 'Make HTTPS Request' steps carry the same Persona-Signature HMAC mechanism.
notes: Docs explicitly recommend API polling over webhooks 'if your application requires instant updates, such as making real-time decisions'.

claim: Sandbox and production environments exist; sandbox performs no real verifications, supports force-pass/force-fail toggles, and the API provides sandbox-only endpoints to Perform Simulate Actions and Set Simulated Data on inquiries; webhook event simulation and sandbox report hit triggering are documented. Production is enabled after contacting Persona to discuss pricing.
notes: Simulate endpoints listed in API reference (perform-simulate-actions, set-simulate-stubs). Testing is forward-looking; there is no documented replay of historical production traffic against a draft policy.

claim: User Audit Logs are retained for up to 6 months and accessible via production API and dashboard: every organization user action records path, method, GET/POST params, IP address, user agent, response status, timestamp, the acting user, session, and impersonator-email-address when applicable.
page_title: List all User Audit Logs (API Reference)
notes: Organization-level resource; intentionally not exposed in sandbox.

claim: RBAC: roles are collections of permissions operating at organization level and environment level (Environments, Product, Data, Development tabs), with per-permission constraints (e.g. restrict Case access to particular templates or assigned users), nested permissions, and default-role assignment. SSO: SAML with Google, Okta, Azure; SCIM provisioning via Okta and Microsoft Entra; 2FA; programmatic role control from the IdP addressed in help docs; multi-organization SSO access supported. SSO is available on Growth and Enterprise plans.
notes: Admin section lists SCIM articles for Okta and Entra. No dedicated maker-checker approval flow for configuration publishing is documented; gating who can publish is achievable via role permissions (inference).

claim: Data minimization and retention controls: redact endpoints exist for inquiries, accounts, cases, reports, transactions (including transaction-biometrics-specific redaction), and verifications; the workflow Redact Object action supports field-level and conditional redaction; API responses and webhook payloads support attribute blocklists and API-key payload filters; and the API spec states that for continuous deletion Persona will 'help you setup a retention policy', with cascading redaction triggered by 'an automated retention policy'.
page_title: Persona OpenAPI spec (accounts redaction description) + Workflows docs
notes: Automated retention policies exist but are configured with Persona's assistance rather than self-serve. Fixed windows: API logs 2 weeks, webhook events 30 days, user audit logs 6 months.

claim: Device and network intelligence is first-class in the API schema: session/device objects expose is-vpn, is-proxy, is-tor, is-datacenter, proxy-type (residential/mobile/corporate/vpn/tor), threat-level, IP latitude/longitude, gps-latitude/gps-longitude/gps-precision, ip-connection-type, ip-isp, and network-organization; a Devices API lists devices; workflows can Trust Device; and Inquiry Signals (org-flag-gated) expose fraud scores such as inquiry/bot_score and inquiry/behavior_threat_level on the API and all inquiry webhooks.
notes: VPN/proxy/Tor fields verified directly in the published OpenAPI spec. GPS plus IP geolocation collected; Persona does not market certified iGaming-grade geolocation like GeoComply (inference from absence in docs).

claim: Persona Marketplace provides ~90+ integrations spanning identity/fraud data providers (LexisNexis InstantID, Mastercard Identity, Prove, SentiLink, Nova Credit, MX, CRS Credit, Clearbit, FullContact, AtData, PhotoDNA, VerifyMy), crypto risk (Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Coinbase, Notabene, Etherscan), auth providers (Auth0, Okta, Clerk, Stytch, WorkOS), CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot), support/comms (Zendesk, Slack, Teams, Twilio), ATS/HRIS platforms, and LLM providers (Anthropic, Google AI, GroqCloud, Replicate). Third-party results surface as native report types with events (e.g. sentilink-scores.ready, equifax-oneview.ready, middesk.ready, kyckr-business-lookup.ready, trm-wallet-screening.ready, chainalysis-address-screening.ready).
notes: Third-party vendor signals are normalized into Persona's unified report/event/workflow-conditional model - direct cross-vendor signal orchestration evidence.

claim: Connect enables cross-organization data sharing between Persona customers via scoped Share Tokens: a source org shares an end user's KYC/KYB data, and the destination org redeems the token to clone/hydrate its own copy, reuse existing results, or run additional verifications and reports; usable via API, SDK, Workflows, or Dashboard, with both orgs responsible for end-user consent.
notes: A network-style reuse mechanism for verification outcomes across organizations.

claim: Persona ships a Solution Library of pre-built packs: Basic Verification, Basic Verification + Address, KYC, KYC + AML, KYC + Age Verification, KYC + Mobile 2FA, KYC + Crypto Watchlist. The KYC Solution bundles one government-ID inquiry template (with selfie liveness), two workflows (post-completion decisioning; failed-inquiry -> auto-create case), and a KYC Manual Review case template; described as 'a starting point for meeting compliance requirements' and fully customizable. Available on all plans.
notes: Packs are technical configuration bundles for compliance use cases; they do not encode jurisdiction-specific statutes and carry no legal-source citations (KYC article explicitly makes no BSA/FinCEN/CIP references).

claim: Pricing: Essential plan at $250/month (annual contract) with 500 free services (verifications/reports)/month then $1.50 per service, self-serve with a 60-day free trial; Growth and Enterprise plans are custom-priced via sales, with Growth adding advanced report/verification types, fraud configurations, Graph, advanced Cases features, and marketplace integrations; Enterprise adds fully customized solutions for organizations with multiple business units/international subsidiaries. A one-year free Startup Program exists. Feature gating documented: Evaluate Code, continuous monitoring, SSO on Growth/Enterprise; API-only integration on Enterprise.
notes: Third-party sources (Vendr/Capterra) report per-verification costs commonly $0.50-$4.00 by type and volume (MEDIUM confidence).

claim: Persona raised a $200M Series D in April 2025 co-led by Founders Fund and Ribbit Capital at a $2B valuation; annual recurring revenue crossed $100M in 2024 with revenue and customer base doubling; more than 4,000 businesses use Persona including OpenAI, LinkedIn, Block, Robinhood, Etsy, and Twilio; platform available in 200+ countries/territories and 20 languages; 300M+ identity verifications completed by 2024.
notes: Corroborated by Yahoo Finance, Biometric Update, FinTech Futures, and Forbes coverage. Series D framing targets 'the verified identity layer for an agentic AI world'.

claim: Persona holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FERPA, Kantara (NIST SP 800-63), and Age Check Certification Scheme certifications, per its security/privacy pages and certification announcements.
page_title: Persona Security, Privacy, and Data Protection Practices
notes: withpersona.com blocked automated fetching (HTTP 403); claim assembled from search-result snippets of the official security page, Persona blog posts (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS), and PR Newswire ISO 27001 announcement. Reduced confidence accordingly.

claim: Third-party analysis (Contrary Research): Persona's automated verification decisions process in roughly 5 seconds; direct competitors include Socure, Jumio, Onfido, with Alloy and Unit21 as adjacent orchestration/case-management players; switching costs are assessed as relatively low (~3-month transition estimate); positioning described as 'the AWS of identity'; 2021 Series C at $1.5B led by Founders Fund; ~$32M revenue and ~575 customers in 2023 per the report's estimates.
page_title: Report: Persona Business Breakdown & Founding Story (Contrary Research)
notes: Pre-Series-D snapshot; revenue/customer figures superseded by 2025 press ($100M+ ARR, 4,000+ businesses). Switching-cost view predates deeper Workflows/Cases/Graph adoption.

claim: Persona's decisioning model is asynchronous: docs advise that 'if your application requires instant updates, such as making real-time decisions... consider using our API to poll for updates instead' of webhooks; workflow runs are created via API and complete asynchronously (response carries status and processing-time-seconds); graph queries are submitted then polled; no synchronous evaluate-rules-and-return-decision endpoint exists anywhere in the 172-path API surface.
notes: Inference (labeled): absence of a synchronous decision endpoint confirmed by review of the complete published OpenAPI path list; Persona is not a sub-second inline authorization engine.

claim: The complete published API surface (172 paths across all dated versions) and the full documentation index contain zero occurrences of ledger, balance, sweepstakes, promotion, prize, winner, loyalty, coupon, or entitlement concepts, and no Terraform/infrastructure-as-code tooling; 'wallet' appears only for crypto-address screening and the Persona Wallet mobile verification mini-app.
notes: Researcher-performed keyword scan of the official machine-readable spec; positive evidence of absence for promotion-administration (A) and ledger/entitlement (F) capability blocks and for IaC support (H10).

claim: As of July 2023 Workflows are scoped at the organization level and run across all of an organization's environments (e.g. Sandbox and Production), part of a broader effort to manage configurations across multiple environments; enterprise plans target organizations with multiple business units and international subsidiaries.
page_title: Workflows: Migration to organization-level Workflows (Help Center)
notes: Multi-environment promotion of config is native; multi-brand is handled via environments/organizations plus per-template theming and custom subdomains.

claim: Age verification is a packaged use case: the Solution Library includes a KYC + Age Verification solution; Persona publishes guidance on age verification laws by industry; and age verification is named as a top use case in developer docs. Persona holds an Age Check Certification Scheme certification per its security page.
page_title: Age Verification Laws by Industry (Persona blog) + Solutions library
notes: Solution existence is official-doc (help center, HIGH); blog page itself was bot-blocked, title/description via search results. Persona is widely reported as an age-assurance provider for large platforms under laws like the UK Online Safety Act (not independently verified in this session).

claim: AI-agent capabilities are appearing in the event model: agent-conversation.created/message-added/errored events and a case.agent-reviewed event ('occurs when a case is reviewed by an agent') exist in the official event catalog, and the Marketplace includes LLM providers (Anthropic, Google AI, GroqCloud, Replicate) for AI-powered workflow steps.
notes: Persona's 2026 releases page (summer26) advertises AI/agent features; page bot-blocked, so scope of agentic review capabilities beyond events is unverified.

claim: Accounts are the persistent per-user/business state container: they group all inquiries, verifications, reports, cases, and documents for an entity; support custom account types, custom fields, and custom statuses; carry tags and typed relations between accounts; support consolidation/deduplication, search, account actions, and bulk import via Importers; reference IDs link repeat interactions to one account.
notes: Custom account types/fields/statuses documented in help center articles NrM9W6KETzMbzQXgdU3cV and 6W3ySuKOa8ez3CEbZYHdcj; relations/tags/consolidation/actions endpoints in API reference index.

claim: Verification inputs are frozen at submission: once a verification reaches submitted status, 'attributes and images can no longer be changed', and Persona then generates check and decision statuses from the VerificationTemplate configuration; verifications can also be investigation-locked/unlocked via dedicated API endpoints.
notes: Input facts for each decision are preserved on the verification/inquiry objects and retrievable via API alongside per-check results.

claim: Evidence export endpoints exist: Print Inquiry PDF, Print Report PDF, and Print Verification PDF API actions, plus a case.exported event and case print-initiated event; SARs export as XML or e-file directly to FinCEN; report history is listable via List Report History.
page_title: Print Inquiry PDF (API Reference) + related export endpoints
notes: Endpoints enumerated in the official API index (llms.txt) and OpenAPI spec.

claim: Official SDKs: JavaScript SDK (v5, with Inlined, React, and Vue variants), iOS SDK (v3), Android SDK (v2), React Native SDK (v2), plus WebView integration guidance, a Persona Wallet mini-app flow (iOS App Clip), and for Relay a server-side SDK, self-hostable Gateway Service, and edge workers (Cloudflare/Vercel). All SDKs have published changelogs and migration guides.
notes: Client-side SDK coverage is deep; no general-purpose server-side API client libraries are documented (API examples are raw HTTP in 8 languages).
